ai.title: Skip terminal execution for single-quote inputs
ai.summary: CLI command execution logic now skips auto-running inputs containing single quotes. This prevents shell interpretation issues during terminal handling. The change updates `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to filter inputs with `'` alongside existing checks for 'error' and word count. `npm-app/knowledge.md` documents the new rule requiring explicit `/run` prefix for such inputs.

eli5.text: The assistant will no longer try to run something that looks like a command if the text you type contains a single quote mark (apostrophe). This is meant to stop the terminal from getting confused by special characters in your input. If you do need something with quotes to run, you'll have to type a special /run prefix first. This is live today for internal testing.

ai.title: Docs MDX pipeline adds CodeDemo plugin and landing polish
ai.summary: ContentLayer now registers `remarkCodeToCodeDemo` from `web/src/lib/remark-code-to-codedemo.ts` in `web/contentlayer.config.ts`, and `web/package.json` adds `@mdx-js/mdx`, `remark-mdx`, `remark-parse`, `remark-stringify`, `to-vfile`, `unified`, `unist-util-visit`, and `vfile-matter` dev dependencies. The web knowledge docs describe writing markdown code blocks instead of direct `CodeDemo` components for consistent styling and copy behavior, while the landing page and docs surfaces receive gradient, layout, and scroll-margin polish. Scope covers `web/src/app/page.tsx`, `web/src/app/docs/[category]/page.tsx`, `web/src/app/docs/layout.tsx`, `web/src/content/help/frameworks.mdx`, `web/src/content/tips/large-projects.mdx`, `backend/knowledge.md`, and `common/src/db/schema.knowledge.md`. The plugin is wired with ContentLayer array syntax `remarkPlugins: [[remarkCodeToCodeDemo]]`, and docs headings use `scroll-mt-24` for anchor offset.

eli5.text: Code examples in the documentation now automatically get styled consistently instead of requiring special formatting each time. When someone writes a code block in the docs, the site will now wrap it in a nice preview box that shows the code with proper styling and includes a one-click copy button. This makes all code examples across the documentation look uniform and easier to use, so you can copy commands or code snippets directly without worrying about formatting differences between pages.

ai.title: Remove NOCOLOR passthrough from terminal.ts
ai.summary: Dropped NO_COLOR env var passthrough in npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts. This stops the PTY from explicitly propagating NO_COLOR, relying on default inheritance instead. FORCE_COLOR remains hardcoded to 1.

eli5.text: The terminal no longer explicitly tells programs to skip colors by removing a setting that passed along the NO_COLOR option. Instead, it now relies on the default behavior of inheriting this setting from your computer. You won't notice any difference unless you specifically rely on NO_COLOR being set in the terminal environment, in which case it will now be handled automatically rather than explicitly.

ai.title: Drop PSModulePath and CI env vars from terminal PTY
ai.summary: Removed PSModulePath and CI from environment config in createPty within npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts. PSModulePath was preserved for PowerShell modules, and CI was passed through for environment detection. This change simplifies the terminal environment setup by eliminating unnecessary variable propagation.

eli5.text: When you open a terminal inside the app, the system used to copy over two environment settings (one for PowerShell modules and one to flag that you were running in a CI/automated environment). Those two settings are no longer forwarded, so the terminal starts up slightly cleaner, but PowerShell module paths and CI detection still work through other means. You wouldn’t see this as a feature, there’s no new behavior to interact with, but if you’ve ever looked at the terminal’s environment variables you’d no longer find those two entries listed at the top of the list. It’s live today and affects anyone using the built-in terminal in the app.
